note.en: This is the fifth section of the 'general discourse' (numbered 'five'), and it closes the whole 'searching out ghosts and spirits' chapter: the earlier parts teach how to tell which ghost or spirit it is, and this teaches what to do once one knows: not to kill, but to invite monks and Daoists to recite scriptures and keep fasts according to the illness. The opening sentence states the position: diviners wrongly judging the gods and offices and sick households believing them and slaughtering animals both use up the household's means, may not cure the illness, and make evil karma for the next life, which even the diviner can hardly escape. It is the same attitude as this chapter's closing passage 'fearing people will judge at random, always worrying that they love killing and waste money' (LY.ILL.EL.43) and the Yi Mao's 'of sacrifice none is better than exorcism, and of exorcism none is better than cultivating oneself' (LY.ILL.YM.63, YM.64). The wording is loose in many places, and the translation marks them: 'liao la jiang' is not a word; the 'Tonglian Scripture' is not known to be any particular scripture; 'nue ji' is the sickness 'nue ji' (malaria), written with a variant character; the character 'fei' in 'can bring about the fei of labour' has an unclear sense, and the translation gives the general sense 'can remove the trouble of labour'; 'Liang Emperor office' should be 'Liang Emperor repentance' (the Liang Emperor precious repentance, a rite to deliver karmic grievances), the original writing 'office' for 'repentance'; 'huo zha ru yi' is not a sentence and is only marked; the 'zhi tu' in 'zhi tu of slaughter, demanding life' is probably 'the six paths' or the like with earlier words missing, and is translated as 'the path of slaughter where the victims demand a life'; 'the animal realm' is the Buddhist 'pang sheng qu' (the realm of animals); 'Tai Sui Yin' is rendered literally; 'Zitong' and 'Great Cavern Honoured Scripture' are transliterated literally; the sentence 'as for those who block water and fire ... and bring on calamity' lists several kinds of conduct that call down misfortune but the book does not go on to give a remedy, and 'starting and destroying' and 'yi wu' are not words either, and the translation marks all of these directly. 'Fire Close day' and 'Fire Receive day' are literal, and are probably the Close and Receive days of the twelve day-spirits, which the book does not explain. 'The hexagrams of the Yi classify the natures of all things, and so cannot all be written out' says that this book has not written out the exorcism of all things in full, and the reader may examine it for himself. Names of gods, spirits, scriptures and rites in this passage are given by transliteration or plain rendering; the book does not explain them, and none is identified here beyond what the book says.

zh: 凡人疾病占问鬼神，术人妄判神司，病家听信宰杀，倾有限之家资，
病未必愈，造来生之恶业，卜亦难逃。
且如瘟疫，系上帝之了剌降，虽日时行亦不善而降殃，
但当合门齐素虔请戒僧持通连经，自得消解。或童男礼拜亦可迪吉。
又如虐疾或有鬼邪，依通书之状式设灶神而可遣。
胎产乃九天圣母所持，延道而诵玉枢经可致临盆之废。
怪病或倚草附木之妖，择僧而念观音经，自是弭灾之法。
冤业相寻，梁皇职可以解，除亡魂出现，地藏经乃能超度。
火殃若降，择火闭日或火收日，延道诵火德经，火乍汝矣！
精魅所临，大则告天师而请法，小则诵真武经而驱遣。
症患膈噎者，惟施食淡口，能超饿鬼。
之途屠宰索命者，独戒杀放生可免，旁生之趣，
又若妄罚誓愿，忤犯天曹，须设斋祭旧而勾消。
若贫难酬愿，可将天曹对疏，叩城隍而回缴，
或富家向许猪羊牛愿后，若贫穷可作粉牲钱马，到天库地库除消亦可。
杜绝兴工动作告土。须按其方隅设坛，无力粉圆可斋殷太岁。
商贾江湖诵三官经，而可保士子功名，
持玉皇经而虔祝药师佛祈当世之延年，金刚经作来生之福利。
祷求嗣续，则建梓童清坛保安，婴幼须念大洞尊经，
至如水火不通或拆桥断路而招谴、左右瘫痪或大秤小斗而生灾。
士庶覆宗盖为毁平冢墓军民绝嗣皆因起灭，社坛非求神而可除，惟改修而可解，
若艺侮神明，须皈依三宝或能求散。
浸占祠宇惟修复，故刹方得安全，
易卦类万物之情因不悉备卜筮通神明之德，自可参详。
yi: 凡是人得了病、占问鬼神的，术士随口乱判是哪位神司，病家听信了就宰杀牲畜，把有限的家财都倾尽了，
病未必好，还给来生造下恶业，占卜的人也难逃。
就说瘟疫，这是上帝降下的了剌（此处原文含混），虽然叫时行，也是因为不善才降下灾殃；
只应全家一起吃素，虔诚地请守戒的僧人持通连经，自然消解，或者请童男礼拜也能引来吉祥。
又如疟疾，或者有鬼邪，依通书的样式设灶神就能送走。
胎产是九天圣母管的，请道士诵玉枢经，可以除去临盆的难处（此处文字含混）。
怪病，或者倚草附木的妖，选僧人念观音经，这自然是平息灾祸的办法。
冤业互相寻找，梁皇忏（原文作「梁皇职」）可以解；有亡魂出现，地藏经才能超度。
火灾如果降下，选火闭日或者火收日，请道士诵火德经，（下面「火乍汝矣」原文含混）。
精魅来临，大的要告天师请法，小的诵真武经驱赶。
得膈噎症的，只要布施食物、吃淡口，能超度饿鬼。
屠宰索命的这一路，只有戒杀放生才能免，这是旁生一趣的事。
又如妄罚誓愿、冒犯天曹的，必须设斋祭奠，勾消旧账。
如果穷得难以还愿，可以向天曹递上对疏，叩城隍退回；
或者富家向神许过猪羊牛的愿，后来穷了，可以做粉牲、纸钱纸马，到天库地库勾消也行。
要杜绝动土兴工惹出的事，要向土地报告，必须按那个方位设坛，没有力量的用粉团斋祭殷太岁。
经商的、走江湖的诵三官经，也能保读书人的功名；
持玉皇经，虔诚祝告药师佛，祈求今世延年；金刚经作来生的福利。
祷求有后，就建梓童清坛保平安；婴幼儿必须念大洞尊经。
至于堵塞水火、拆桥断路而招来谴责，左右瘫痪或者大秤小斗而生出灾祸的，（此处原文没有说办法）
士人百姓宗族覆灭，大多是毁平了坟墓；军民绝嗣，都是因为「起灭」（此处含混）；社坛不是求神能除的，只有改修才能解；
如果侮慢神明，必须皈依三宝，或许能求得消散。
侵占祠宇的，只有修复，旧庙才能安全。
易卦分类万物的情状，不能全部写备，卜筮通神明的德，自然可以自己参详。
en: When people fall ill and divine about ghosts and spirits, the diviners wrongly judge the gods and offices at random, the sick household believes them and slaughters animals, exhausting its limited household means,
the illness is not necessarily cured, evil karma is made for the next life, and the diviner too can hardly escape it.
Take epidemic: it is a descent from the Supreme Emperor, the 'liao la' (the text is garbled here), and though called seasonal, it too descends as calamity because of what is not good;

one should have the whole household eat vegetarian together and reverently invite a monk who keeps the precepts to recite the Tonglian Scripture, and it dissolves of itself, or boys performing worship can also lead to good fortune.
Again, malaria, or where there are ghosts and evil: following the forms of the almanac, set up the Kitchen God and it can be sent away.
Childbirth is presided over by the Holy Mother of the Nine Heavens; invite a Daoist to recite the Yushu Scripture, which can remove the trouble of labour (the wording is loose).
For strange illnesses, or the demons that lean on grass and cling to trees, choose a monk to chant the Guanyin Scripture; this is naturally the way to still calamity.
Where grievances and karma pursue each other, the Liang Emperor rite (the text has 'Liang Emperor office') can resolve it; where a dead soul appears, the Earth Store Scripture can deliver it.
If a fire calamity descends, choose a Fire Close day or a Fire Receive day and invite a Daoist to recite the Fire Virtue Scripture (the words that follow, 'huo zha ru yi', are garbled).
Where sprites and spectres have come, if great, appeal to the Heavenly Master to request rites, and if small, recite the Zhenwu Scripture to drive them away.
For one whose illness is a choking obstruction of the gullet, only give food and keep a bland mouth, which can deliver the hungry ghosts.
For the path of slaughter where the victims demand a life, only abstaining from killing and releasing life can avoid it; it is a matter of the animal realm.
Again, those who rashly swear oaths and vows and offend the Heavenly Bureau must set a fast and offering to cancel the old debt.
If too poor to redeem the vow, one may present a memorial to the Heavenly Bureau and kowtow to the City God to return it;

or a rich family that vowed pigs, sheep and oxen to the gods and has since grown poor can make flour animals, paper money and paper horses, and cancelling at the Heavenly Treasury and Earthly Treasury will also do.

To stop the trouble from starting building work and digging, report to the Earth, and one must set up an altar according to that quarter; those without means offer flour balls as a fast to Tai Sui Yin.
Merchants and those on rivers and lakes recite the Three Officials Scripture, which can also protect scholars' careers;
reciting the Jade Emperor Scripture and reverently praying to the Medicine Buddha seeks long life in this world; the Diamond Sutra makes blessings for the next life.
To pray for an heir, one builds a pure altar to Zitong for safety; for infants one must recite the Great Cavern Honoured Scripture.

As for those who block water and fire or demolish bridges and cut roads and so invite reproach, those with paralysis of left and right, or those who use large scales and small measures and so bring on calamity (the text gives no remedy here),

the overturning of a lineage among gentry and commoners is mostly from levelling tombs, and the lack of heirs among soldiers and people is all from 'starting and destroying' (garbled here); an earth altar cannot be removed by praying to the gods, and only rebuilding can resolve it;
if one has insulted the gods, one must take refuge in the Three Jewels and may perhaps seek dispersal.
For encroaching on a shrine, only restoration, and then the old temple is safe.
The hexagrams of the Yi classify the natures of all things and cannot all be written out in full; divination communicates with the virtue of the spirits, and one may examine it for oneself.

title: 请僧道看应爻：以应爻为主、福德为凭；应上子孙（福德）是受戒善士，父母是法术精专，官鬼是神鬼钦服；兄弟是奸欺伪妄多阻误，妻财是贪利好色、非通天之流；子孙临白虎是恶辈，福德带青龙是善人

rule.yi: 请僧接道是为了招请贤者，要看的是应爻上站着什么。以应爻为主，以福德（子孙）为凭。应爻上是子孙（福德），这个僧道确实是受了戒、有行持的善人；父母临着应，法术精深专一；官鬼临着应，神鬼都敬服；兄弟临着应，多奸诈虚伪、常常阻误；妻财临着应，是贪婪图利、好色营财的人，不是能通天彻地的人。子孙临白虎，是恶人，心里容不下凶险；福德带青龙，是善人，有慈善，心里常存德行。占卦只看应爻，就知道休咎。
rule.en: To invite monks and Daoists in order to summon the worthy, look at what stands on the Other line. The Other line is the main line, and Output (the fortune spirit) is the ground. Output on the Other line: he is a good man who has received the precepts and has real conduct; Resource on it: his rites and arts are refined and exclusive; Pressure on it: gods and ghosts admire and submit; Peer on it: crafty, deceitful and false, and often blocking and erring; Wealth on it: a man greedy for profit, lustful and scheming for wealth, not one of those who penetrate heaven and earth. Output on the White Tiger is a wicked man; Output (the fortune spirit) with the Azure Dragon is a good man, compassionate, whose heart always keeps virtue. In divining, look only at the Other line, and one knows good and ill.

note.yi: 这一章说的是请僧道做法事时，怎么看请来的这位僧道是贤是愚。章首小标是「以应爻为主，福德为凭」：占的是「所请的僧道」这个人，他站在应爻上，所以看应爻和它上面的六亲、六神。和这本书别的章一样，先是歌诀、再是解说；这里的解说文字多处含混，译文里标出。「职悔业根」按上下文读作「忏悔业根」；「慈惠降龙」「有法灵伏虎」用的是僧道降龙伏虎的典故，只按字面译；「以亲污积」不成句；「乃鄙入蝎荤」按「乃鄙人〔嗜〕荤」的大意译，并标含混；「盗助」「欺人机有慈善」都不成句，译文里保留并标出。「福德在时」的福德就是子孙，所以「子孙乃僧道也」和「福德即子孙也」是一个意思：子孙在这里既是福德、又是僧道本人。 这一段里神、经、法事的名字，书里没有解释，这里按字面译或音译，不作认定。
note.en: This chapter is about how to tell, when inviting monks and Daoists to perform rites, whether the one invited is worthy or foolish. The chapter's subtitle is 'the Other line is the main line, and Output is the ground': what is divined is the monk or Daoist invited, who stands on the Other line, so one looks at the Other line and the six relations and six spirits on it. As in the book's other chapters, verse comes first and then the commentary; the commentary here is loose in many places, and the translation marks them. 'Zhi hui ye gen' is read as 'repenting the roots of karma' from the context; 'the compassionate ones who subdue dragons' and 'the efficacious ones who subdue tigers' use the tale of monks and Daoists subduing dragons and tigers, and are translated only literally; 'yi qin wu ji' is not a sentence; 'nai bi ru xie hun' is translated in the general sense of 'a base man craving meat', and marked as garbled; 'dao zhu' and 'qi ren ji you ci shan' are not sentences, and the translation keeps them and marks them. The 'fortune spirit' in 'when the fortune spirit is present' is Output, so 'Output is the monk or Daoist' and 'the fortune spirit is Output' mean the same thing: Output here is both the fortune spirit and the monk or Daoist himself. Names of gods, spirits, scriptures and rites in this passage are given by transliteration or plain rendering; the book does not explain them, and none is identified here beyond what the book says.

yi: 以应爻为主，以福德为凭。
en: The Other line is the main line, and Output (the fortune spirit) is the ground.

yi: 迎请僧人、接待道士是为了招请贤者，
却要看是什么人站在应爻里。
en: In inviting monks and receiving Daoists to summon the worthy,
look instead at who stands on the Other line.

zh: 有念佛行善因果法缘、或祈福寿、或职悔业根，
如修斋设法、如炼度书符，
而僧人有慈惠降龙道士，
yi: 人活在世上，
有念佛行善、因果法缘的，或者祈求福寿的，或者忏悔业根的，
比如修斋设法、炼度书符，
都是想使活着的和亡故的人得利，
免不了要迎接僧道，
而僧人里有慈悲降龙的，道士里
有法灵伏虎的，
都靠宣扬梵语，
礼拜诵经，
必定能扶持纲常、树立纪律，
才可以入圣超凡。
如果请来的不好，
迎接的不是贤人，
就会搅乱坛场，混淆荤素的坛，
亵渎斋醮的筵席，
沾上污秽的积累（此处含混），
这样就没有感应，
白白摆出了诚意。
占卦只看应爻，
就知道休咎。
en: A person living in the world
may have the karmic bonds of reciting the Buddha's name and doing good, or pray for blessing and long life, or repent the roots of karma,
such as holding fasts and setting up rites, refining and delivering, and writing talismans;
all wish to benefit the living and the dead,
and one cannot but invite monks and Daoists;
and among monks there are compassionate ones who subdue dragons, among Daoists
efficacious ones who subdue tigers,
all by proclaiming Sanskrit chants
and reciting scriptures in worship;
they surely can support the norms and establish the code,
and only then can enter the sacred and transcend the ordinary.
If those invited are not good,
and those welcomed are not worthy,
they will disorder the altar grounds and confuse the meat-eating altar,
profane the ritual feast,
and take on accumulated impurity (garbled here);
this has no response,
and one has set out sincerity in vain.
In divining, look only at the Other line,
and one knows good and ill.

yi: 福德在的时候是真的持戒有行，
父母、官鬼居在那里的，法术精通。
en: When Output is present, the precepts are truly kept;
where Resource or Pressure sits, the rites are thoroughly mastered.

yi: 就是说，如果子孙在应爻上，
一定是受过戒的善士，
有行持的真人。
父母临着它的，
必定法术精专。
官鬼临着它的，
必定神鬼都敬服。
en: That is, if Output is on the Other line,
he is surely a good man who has received the precepts,
a true person of conduct.
Where Resource sits on it,
his rites and arts are surely refined and exclusive.
Where Pressure sits on it,
gods and ghosts surely admire and submit.

yi: 兄爻值在这里，大多奸诈虚伪；
财象临在他身上，喜欢牟利经营。
en: Peer sitting here is mostly crafty and false;
the Wealth image sitting on him likes profit and scheming.

zh: 迎真籍道之法力以赞参。
兄弟应值则奸欺而伪妄，
yi: 供奉佛的时候，
靠僧人的慈悲之因，来（此处含混）助成。
迎接真人，靠道士的法力来赞助参与。
兄弟值在应位，就奸诈欺骗、虚伪妄言，
多阻碍失误，废掉更改。
妻财监临这个人，是贪婪图利的，
好色营财，
是卑鄙、（此处含混）荤腥的人，
不是通天彻地的一类。
en: In making offerings to the Buddha,
one relies on the monk's compassionate cause, to [garbled] and help it succeed.
In welcoming the true one, one relies on the Daoist's power of rites to assist the taking part.
If Peer holds the Other position, he is crafty, deceitful and false,
often blocking and erring, and spoiling the change.
If Wealth oversees the man, he is greedy and seeks profit,
lustful and scheming for wealth,
a base man, [garbled] meat and rank food,
not of the kind who penetrate heaven and earth.

yi: 恶辈：子孙临着白虎；
善人：福德带着青龙。
en: A wicked one: Output on the White Tiger;
a good man: Output (the fortune spirit) with the Azure Dragon.

zh: 其心不胜凶险立行匪凡善良。
yi: 子孙就是僧道，
白虎贴着守着，
他的心受不住凶险，举止行为不是寻常的善良。
福德就是子孙，
青龙卫护着，
那人天性有慈善，（此处原文有误）
心里常存德行。
en: Output is the monk or Daoist;
with the White Tiger attached and guarding,
his heart cannot bear danger, and his conduct is not that of the ordinary good.
Output (the fortune spirit) is Output;
with the Azure Dragon protecting,
the man is by nature compassionate (the original has a slip here),
and his heart always keeps virtue.

title: 请僧道法事成不成：官绝则神天不纳、六冲则僧道无缘（六冲不用）；子孙冲破则诵经如诳语、应空则礼忏如虚文、无子则忏礼徒然；官爻主设醮之场、无鬼无因果、官空无德无功；子旺则斋坛功德无亏、福德掌醮功程有力；福动化鬼、官来克世则作福反凶（求亲反疏、求荣反辱）

rule.yi: 法事成不成，要看几个关口：官鬼绝，神天不接受；卦是六冲，僧道没有缘分，所以六冲的卦不用。子孙用神管着自家的事，诵经宣偈要念得琳琅悦耳，如果遇到冲破，就只是白诵、成了谎话；僧道所在的应位是占卜人的用神，金经实偈要诚敬地宣扬，如果被冲，就白念、成了虚文；应爻落空，穿着袈裟礼拜也没有用，没有子孙，忏悔礼拜也是徒然。官爻主设醮的场地，没有鬼就没有因果，官空就没有德也没有功；子孙乘旺，斋坛的功德没有亏欠；福德掌管醮事，主事功有力。设斋修善的时候，福动却变成了鬼，就是想亲近反而疏远了；作福祈恩的时候，官鬼来克世爻，就是求荣反而得辱——都是要人感应、用心与天神相合，怎么可以亵渎而不加谨慎呢。
rule.en: Whether the rite succeeds depends on several points: if the Pressure line is cut off, the gods and heaven do not accept; if the hexagram is a Six-Clash, monks and Daoists have no affinity, so a Six-Clash hexagram is not used. Output as the Subject governs the affairs of my household, and reciting scriptures and proclaiming verses must be delivered in ringing tones; if it meets clash or break, the reciting is in vain and becomes lying words; the Other position of the monk or Daoist is the Subject of the one divining, and the golden scriptures and true verses must be proclaimed with sincerity and reverence; if it is clashed, the reciting is wasted and becomes an empty text; if the Other line is Void, what use is the robe and the bowing, and if there is no Output, penance and prostration are in vain. The Pressure line governs the site of the ritual; with no ghost there is no cause and effect, and with the Pressure line Void there is no virtue and no merit; with Output riding strength, the merit of the fast altar has no deficiency; Output holds the power of the ritual, and the work has strength. In holding a fast and cultivating good, if Output moves and changes into a ghost, then seeking closeness one grows distant; in performing blessing rites and praying for grace, if the Pressure line comes to control the Self, one seeks honour and gets shame instead; all of it asks for response and for the heart to accord with the heavenly gods, so how may one profane it without taking care?

note.yi: 这一节接上一条（LY.ILL.EL.55）：上一条看请来的僧道是贤是愚，这一条看这场法事能不能成。它的判据基本是熟悉的：官鬼是神天的受纳（官绝则神天不纳）、子孙是诵经念偈的功德（子孙被冲破则徒诵）、应爻是僧道本人（应空则礼忏无益）、六冲是缘分散（六冲不用），福动化鬼、官来克世则作福反凶。「六冲」在这里的意思是「缘散」，和别处的用法（六冲卦病易消，LY.ILL.EL.22）不同——这里是说法事不宜遇六冲。「神天不纳因官绝」的「官绝」是官鬼绝。「鹤憋忏礼」的「鹤憋」不成词，译文里标出；「设旧」疑是「设醮」的误写，译作「holding the ritual」；「修齐」是「修斋」；「鬼煞临斋坛之事」不成句，译文标出；「谄之而不蒙福媚之而反见遭用人感应」一句文字散乱，译文只译出能读的部分。这一节的说理是：要人感应、要用心，所以不能亵渎神明而不谨慎。 这一段里神、经、法事的名字，书里没有解释，这里按字面译或音译，不作认定。
note.en: This section follows the previous entry (LY.ILL.EL.55): the previous one looks at whether the monk or Daoist invited is worthy or foolish, and this one looks at whether the rite can succeed. Its criteria are mostly familiar: the Pressure line is the acceptance by the gods and heaven (with the Pressure line cut off, the gods and heaven do not accept); Output is the merit of reciting scriptures and verses (with Output clashed or broken the reciting is in vain); the Other line is the monk or Daoist himself (with the Other line Void, penance is of no use); the Six-Clash scatters affinity (the Six-Clash is not used); and with Output moving and changing into a ghost, or the Pressure line controlling the Self, blessing rites bring misfortune instead. 'Six-Clash' here means 'affinity scattered', which differs from its use elsewhere (a Six-Clash hexagram makes an illness easy to dispel, LY.ILL.EL.22): here it says that a rite should not meet the Six-Clash. The 'guan jue' in 'because the Pressure line is cut off' is the Pressure line cut off. 'He bie chan li' contains 'he bie', which is not a word, and the translation marks it; 'she jiu' is probably a slip for 'she jiao' (holding the ritual), and is translated as 'holding the ritual'; 'xiu qi' is 'xiu zhai' (cultivating the fast); 'the ghost killing sits on the affairs of the fast altar' is not a sentence, and the translation marks it; the sentence 'flattering it brings no blessing, fawning on it one instead meets ... response' is scattered in wording, and only the readable part is translated. The reasoning of this section is: one must have response and must have the heart, and so one may not profane the gods without taking care. Names of gods, spirits, scriptures and rites in this passage are given by transliteration or plain rendering; the book does not explain them, and none is identified here beyond what the book says.

yi: 神和天不接纳，是因为官鬼断绝；
僧道没有缘分，是因为六冲。
en: The gods and heaven do not accept, because the Pressure line is cut off;
monks and Daoists have no affinity, because of the Six-Clash.

zh: 如官爻值缘人徒尔叩天而天不受，
僧有善缘而凡人因无缘法，
盖缘卦值并冲道多缘法，
而斋主为没因缘良为爻生冲激，
yi: 道场是善事，
必须一片诚意才能感通。
如果官爻值在有缘的人上，白白叩天，天也不接受；
僧人有善缘，而凡人因为没有缘法；
大概是卦里值了冲，道多缘法，（此处含混）
而斋主没有因缘，好像是爻生出冲激的缘故，
所以六冲不用。
en: A ritual ground is a good work,
and needs a single sincerity to move the powers.
If the Pressure line meets the affinity person, he kowtows to heaven in vain and heaven does not accept it;
the monk has good affinity, but the ordinary man lacks the destined bond;
it is probably that the hexagram holds a clash, and the Way has many affinities (garbled here),
while the sponsor has no karmic tie, as if from the lines producing clash and agitation,
and so the Six-Clash is not used.

yi: 子孙被破，诵经宣讲就像说谎；
应爻落空，礼忏拜跪就像一阵风。
en: Output broken, reciting scriptures and proclaiming them is like lying;
the Other line Void, penance and prostration are like the wind.

zh: 诵经宣偈全要琳琅讽念，
若逢冲破则徒诵之而为诳语矣！
僧道应位为占主之用神，
yi: 子孙用神管着我家的事，
诵经宣偈全要像琳琅一样清越地念诵，
如果遇上冲破，那就是白诵、成了谎话了！
僧道所在的应位是占卜人的用神，
金经实偈要诚敬地宣扬。
如果遇上被冲，
那就是白念、成了虚文了！
应爻落空，那袈裟礼拜有什么用？
没有子孙，那（此处含混）忏礼也是白费。
en: Output as the Subject governs the affairs of my household;
reciting scriptures and proclaiming verses must be delivered in ringing, jade-like tones;
if it meets clash or break, the reciting is in vain and has become lying words!
The monk's or Daoist's Other position is the Subject of the one divining;
the golden scriptures and true verses are proclaimed with sincerity and reverence.
If it meets being clashed,
the reciting is wasted and becomes an empty text!
If the Other line is Void, what use is the robe and the bowing?
If there is no Output, then the [garbled] penance and prostration are also in vain.

yi: 官鬼落空，设醮没有因果；
子孙旺相，修斋有大功。
en: The ghost Void, holding the ritual has no cause and effect;
Output strong, cultivating the fast has great merit.

yi: 官爻主管设醮的场地，
没有鬼就没有因也没有果，
鬼煞临在斋坛的事上（此处含混）。
官爻落空，
那有什么德、什么功？
子孙乘着旺，
斋坛的功德没有亏欠。
福德掌管醮事，
主管功程有力。
en: The Pressure line governs the site of the ritual;
with no ghost there is no cause and no effect;
the ghost killing sits on the affairs of the fast altar (garbled here).
If the Pressure line is Void,
what virtue is there, what merit?
If Output rides strength,
the merit of the fast altar has no deficiency.
Output holds the power of the ritual,
and governs the work having strength.

yi: 福变成了鬼爻，官鬼克世，
不但作福，反而遭凶。
en: Output changing into a Pressure line, or the Pressure line controlling the Self,
not only no blessing, but misfortune instead.

zh: 谄之而不蒙福媚之而反见遭用人感应，
yi: 设斋修善，
福动却变成鬼，
那就是想亲近反而疏远了！
作福祈求恩典，
官鬼来克世爻，
那就是求荣耀反而受辱了！
谄媚它却得不到福，巴结它反而遭到（此处含混）感应，
用心要与天神相符合，
感通要合于天理的回应，
怎么可以亵渎而不加谨慎呢？
en: In holding a fast and cultivating good,
if Output moves and changes into a ghost,
then seeking closeness one grows distant!
In performing blessing rites and praying for grace,
if the Pressure line comes to control the Self,
one seeks honour and gets shame instead!
flattering it brings no blessing, fawning on it one instead meets [garbled] response;
the heart must accord with the heavenly gods,
and the moving of them must accord with the reply of heavenly principle;
how may one profane it without taking care?

title: 还赛解厄：以福神为主、用象为凭；因灾酬愿寻福德、凶吉再辨用爻是否得令；用弱忌兴灾未退、忌衰用旺患能消；父母动克子则洪恩浅、财动生官则邪魅招；世旺子强官受制则祭神之后别无妖、赛神后保平安、解厄后无咎

rule.yi: 酬愿还赛、解厄，以福神（子孙）为主，以用象为凭。因为遭了灾要酬愿，就找福德；吉凶还要辨用爻得不得令。用爻弱而忌神兴，灾没有退；忌神衰而用爻旺，病患能消。父母发动克子孙，恩典浅薄承受不住；财爻发动生官鬼，邪魅就招来了。世爻旺、子孙强、官鬼受制，祭神之后就再没有妖祟；世是自己，旺则病必痊愈，子孙是福，强则压住鬼祟——这个强了，别的就必弱，福旺鬼将除，赛神之后保平安，解厄完了没有咎，禳解就吉，请祷就没有殃。
rule.en: In redeeming vows and lifting calamity, Output (the fortune spirit) is the main line and the Subject image is the ground. Because of a calamity one redeems a vow, so look to Output; for ill or good one must still distinguish whether the Subject line has gained or lost the season. With the Subject weak and the Adversary rising, the calamity has not retreated; with the Adversary weak and the Subject strong, the affliction can dissolve. If Resource moves and controls Output, the great grace is shallow and cannot be borne; if Wealth moves and generates Pressure, evil spirits are invited. With the Self strong, Output strong and the Pressure line held in check, after sacrificing to the gods there is no further evil; the Self is me, and if strong the illness will surely be cured; Output is fortune, and if strong it suppresses the ghostly haunting, and where this is strong the rest must be weak: the fortune strong, the ghost is about to be removed; after giving thanks to the gods peace is assured, when lifting the calamity is done there is no blame, and exorcism then is auspicious and petitioning and praying has no misfortune.

note.yi: 章首小标是「以福神为主，用象为凭」——福神就是子孙。这一章说的是「酬愿还赛、解厄」这类事：遭了灾或病去还愿、谢神，怎么看能不能成。这一章的判据是本书常见的一套：子孙（福神）强、官鬼受制，还赛就吉；父母克子孙、财生官，则不吉。「用弱忌兴」「忌衰用旺」和本书前面的用神、忌神读法一致（LY.ILL.EL.22：忌神旺发患多年）；「世旺则病必安痊，子强则压制鬼祟」是把世爻当作自己、子孙当作能压鬼的福。原文「惟子卦无凶，寻福德占爻则吉」的「子卦」按「子孙一卦」译，读法没有把握；「邹眉」是「皱眉」；「无青咎」的「青」字费解，疑是「责」（无责咎），这里保留原字并标出；「洪恩」是大恩（上天的恩典）。这一章没有说「还赛要不要杀牲」，和上一节（LY.ILL.EL.54）的立场并不冲突。 这一段里神、经、法事的名字，书里没有解释，这里按字面译或音译，不作认定。
note.en: The chapter's subtitle is 'Output (the fortune spirit) is the main line and the Subject image is the ground' — the fortune spirit is Output. This chapter is about redeeming vows and giving thanks and lifting calamity: how to tell, when one redeems a vow or thanks the gods after a calamity or illness, whether it will succeed. Its criteria are a set common in this book: with Output (the fortune spirit) strong and the Pressure line held in check, redeeming the vow is auspicious; with Resource controlling Output and Wealth generating Pressure, it is not. 'Subject weak and Adversary rising' and 'Adversary weak and Subject strong' are consistent with the book's earlier reading of the Subject and the Adversary (LY.ILL.EL.22: the Adversary strong and moving makes an affliction of many years); 'the Self strong and the illness will surely be cured, Output strong and it suppresses the ghostly haunting' takes the Self as oneself and Output as the fortune that can press down the ghost. In the original 'as long as Output has no ominous sign, look to the divined line where Output sits', 'zi gua' (translated 'Output') is read as the Output hexagram, and the reading is not certain; 'zou mei' is 'zhou mei' (knitted brows); the 'qing' in 'wu qing jiu' is hard to understand and is probably 'ze' (blame), and here the original character is kept and marked; 'hong en' is great grace (heaven's grace). This chapter does not say whether redeeming a vow calls for slaughter, and this does not conflict with the position of the previous section (LY.ILL.EL.54). Names of gods, spirits, scriptures and rites in this passage are given by transliteration or plain rendering; the book does not explain them, and none is identified here beyond what the book says.

yi: 以福神为主，以用象为凭。
en: Output (the fortune spirit) is the main line, and the Subject image is the ground.

yi: 因为灾祸要酬愿，就寻福德；
吉凶还要辨别用爻。
en: For a calamity, redeeming a vow, look to Output;
for ill or good, one must still distinguish the Subject line.

zh: 因罹患而祟鬼为殃则酬谢之。
又当辨用爻之失令得令，
yi: 人的身体有五脏，
天的气有六经，调摄得好的就安，
失和的就生病；
但是染上灾祸而星辰不顺的，
就向它们祈祷。
因为遭了患难而是祟鬼作殃的，就酬谢它。
许下的愿应当还赛，对神有利；
只要子孙这一卦没有凶，
寻福德所在的占爻就吉。
又要分辨用爻是失令还是得令，
才能使占卜的人皱着的眉头舒开。
en: The human body has five viscera,
and the heavens' qi has six channels; those who regulate them well are at peace,
those out of harmony fall ill;
but if one is infected with calamity and the stars are unfavourable,
one prays to them.
If, having met misfortune, a haunting ghost is the calamity, one gives thanks to it.
A vow made should be redeemed, and the thanksgiving benefits the gods;
as long as Output has no ominous sign,
looking to the divined line where Output sits is auspicious.
One must also distinguish whether the Subject line has lost or gained the season,
so as to make the knitted brows of the one divining relax.

yi: 用爻弱而忌神兴，灾还没有退；
忌神衰而用爻旺，病患能消。
en: The Subject weak and the Adversary rising, the calamity has not retreated;
the Adversary weak and the Subject strong, the affliction can dissolve.

yi: 是说我所占的人是用神，
而用神休囚薄弱，
它的形势就危险了！
而所忌的爻在害它，
如果这害又发动兴旺，
那有谁能抵挡呢？
灾祸过失还没有退，
厄患还没有解。
忌神如果衰弱，
病症就可以消除。
用爻如果旺相，
灾病立刻痊愈。
en: It means that the person I divine about is the Subject,
and if the Subject is resting, trapped and weak,
its situation is perilous!
And the line that is feared does harm,
and if this harm moves and rises,
who can resist it?
The calamity and fault have not retreated,
and the affliction has not been resolved.
If the Adversary is weak,
the illness can be dispelled.
If the Subject line is strong,
the illness is cured at once.

yi: 父母兴动克子孙，大恩就浅；
财爻发动生官鬼，邪魅就招来。
en: Resource rising and controlling Output, the great grace is shallow;
Wealth moving and generating Pressure, evil spirits are invited.

yi: 父母发动能克子孙，
纵然有上天的恩典，也薄弱低劣、难以承受。
财爻兴动就生官鬼，
怎么会没有鬼邪张扬作祸呢？
en: If Resource moves and can control Output,
then even if there is heaven's grace, it is thin and poor and hard to receive.
If the Wealth line rises it generates Pressure;
how could there be no blustering of ghosts and evil making misfortune?

yi: 世爻旺、子孙强、官鬼受制，
祭神之后别的再没有妖祟。
en: The Self strong and Output strong, the Pressure line held in check,
after sacrificing to the gods there is no further evil.

yi: 世爻是我，
旺就病一定安然痊愈。
子孙是福，
强就压制鬼祟，
意思是说这个强，其余的必弱，
福旺鬼就将被除去，
赛神之后保平安，
解厄结束的时候没有（青）咎，
禳解就吉，请祷就没有殃。
en: The Self is me;
if strong, the illness will surely be fully cured.
Output is fortune;
if strong it suppresses the ghostly haunting;
the idea being that where this is strong, the rest must be weak:
the fortune strong, the ghost is about to be removed;
after giving thanks to the gods, peace is assured;
when lifting the calamity is done there is no blame ('qing jiu', the first character probably a slip),
exorcism then is auspicious, and petitioning and praying has no misfortune.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·胜光（月建午）占病：怪病气冲天、十生九死；司命溪河伤亡家先作祟宜禳度；午宫卦断大煞临门宜退谢、板木来全替去病

rule.yi: 月建落在午、叫胜光的时候占病：病来得古怪，气往上冲，十个里有九个要死，活下来的也拖得很久；心里结着热，气息紊乱急促，又添疼痛，病情难说。作祟的是司命、溪河一类的神，和横死的亡魂、家里的祖先，要禳解超度。后面「午宫卦断」另有一段：大煞到了门上，适合送走它并还愿答谢；社司和朝鬼拖累病人好几年；板木来齐了替他，病就去了，病人慢慢平安痊愈。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Wu, named Shengguang, divining illness: the illness is strange, the breath surging up to the sky, nine of ten die and the one who lives lingers on; heat knots in the heart, the breath is disordered and hurried, pain is added, and the illness is hard to describe. The ones at work are spirits such as Siming and the streams and rivers, the dead by injury, and the household ancestors, and rites of averting and deliverance are called for. A further passage after 'the verdict for the Wu-palace hexagrams' says: the Great Killer is at the door, and it is fitting to dismiss it and give thanks; the Altar Official and the Court ghosts drag on for years; when the wooden boards have come, complete, to stand in for him, the illness goes and the sick person gradually finds peace and cure.

note.yi: 这一条是「论十月将值日要决」十二首里的第一首。十二首的格式一样：先是小标题（某将值日，括号里写月建），然后是一首七言诗，前半写这个月份占病的症状和作祟的是谁，中间插一句「某宫卦断」，后半是这一宫的卦怎么断、怎么禳解。标题写的是「十月将」，实际列了十二将，从午（胜光）排起，到巳（太乙）为止，每将对着一个月（午=五月……巳=四月）；标题说「值日」，括号里写的却是「月建」「某月之事」，所以这里按月份读，书没有说日和月是怎么换算的。  这一首里的几个词书里都没有解释，译文只照字面：「司命」是掌管命运的神（民间也指灶神，书里另有「灶司」）；「伤亡」是横死、受伤而死的亡魂，「家先」是家里的祖先，「大煞」是一种凶煞，「社司」是社（土地神坛）的神，「朝鬼」不知所指；「板木」不知是什么，按上下文像是做法事时用来替身的木板（下一首说「板木未全凶怪梦」，板木没备齐就凶），这是读法，不是书里写的。「气舛急」的「舛」字按上下文读作气息紊乱，「怪病」的「怪」是说病来得古怪、像撞了什么，不是一个病名。「午宫卦断」书里没有说是指哪些卦，译文只写「午宫的卦」。
note.en: This is the first of the twelve pieces of the 'essentials of the month-generals ruling the day'. All twelve have the same form: a small heading (so-and-so rules the day, with the Month in brackets), then a seven-character verse whose first half gives the symptoms of this month's illness and who is at work, with a line 'the verdict for such-and-such palace hexagrams' in the middle, and a second half on how hexagrams of that palace are judged and how the matter is averted. The title says 'ten month-generals' but twelve are listed, from Wu (Shengguang) to Si (Taiyi), each answering to a month (Wu = the fifth month ... Si = the fourth month); the heading says 'rules the day' but the brackets speak of the Month and of 'the matters of such-and-such month', so the verses are read here by month, and the book does not say how day and month are converted.  Several words in this verse are not explained in the book and are rendered only literally: 'Siming' is the god in charge of fates (in popular religion also the Kitchen God, and the book elsewhere writes 'the Kitchen Official'); 'the dead by injury' are the souls of those who died violently or by wounds, 'the household ancestors' are the family's dead, 'the Great Killer' is a kind of fierce killer, 'the Altar Official' is the spirit of the village altar, and what the 'Court ghosts' are is not known; what the 'wooden boards' are is not known either, and in context they look like boards used as stand-ins in a rite (the next verse says 'when the wooden boards are not complete it is ominous, with strange dreams'), which is a reading and not what the book writes. In 'the breath is disordered and hurried' the character rendered 'disordered' is read from context; the 'strange' of 'strange illness' says the illness comes in an uncanny way, as if something had been run into, and is not the name of a disease. The book does not say which hexagrams 'the Wu-palace hexagrams' are, and the translation says only 'the Wu-palace hexagrams'.

zh: （月建值午则知胜光上卦所生）
yi: 胜光当值的日子
（月建落在午上，就知道胜光在卦上生出的事。）
胜光当值时得病古怪，气往上冲天；
十个里有九个要死，活下来的也久久不好；
心里结着热，气息紊乱急促；
再加上疼痛加重，病情难以说清；
司命、溪河这些神鬼，要去禳解超度；
横死的亡魂作祸，还牵连到家里的祖先；
午宫的卦这样断：
大煞到了门上，适合送走它并还愿答谢；
社司和朝鬼，拖累病人好几年；
板木来齐了替他，病就去了；
病人慢慢得到平安痊愈。
en: When Shengguang rules the day
(when the Month falls on Wu, know what Shengguang gives rise to in the hexagram)
Shengguang: the illness is strange, the breath surging up to the sky;
of ten, nine die, and the one who lives lingers on;
heat knots in the heart and the breath is disordered and hurried;
pain is added besides, and the illness is hard to describe;
Siming and the streams and rivers: seek to avert and release them by rites;
the dead by injury make trouble, and it reaches the household ancestors;
The verdict for the Wu-palace hexagrams:
the Great Killer is at the door: it is fitting to dismiss it and give thanks;
the Altar Official and the Court ghosts drag on for years;
the wooden boards come, complete, to stand in for him, and the illness goes;
and the sick person gradually finds peace and cure.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·小吉（月建未）占病：头痛、三焦热闷腹疼、浑身沉重；墓杀最凶；未宫卦断伤亡死鬼土地作祟、请巫师禳让药方通

rule.yi: 月建落在未、叫小吉的时候占病：头痛，三焦发热发闷，腹中疼痛，全身沉重，难以起身；飞来的墓杀最凶；卯方得的病会绕一圈又回来。「未宫卦断」那一段说：作祟的是横死的亡魂、死去的鬼和土地，让病人说胡话；板木没有备齐，就凶，多怪梦；要请巫师禳解让退，药方才通。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Wei, named Xiaoji, divining illness: headache, heat and oppression in the Triple Burner, pain in the belly, the whole body heavy so that he can hardly rise; the Tomb Killer that flies in is the most ominous; an illness taken in the Mao direction goes around and comes back. The passage 'the verdict for the Wei-palace hexagrams' says: the ones at work are the dead by injury, the dead ghosts and the Earth God, making the patient talk deliriously; if the wooden boards are not complete it is ominous, with strange dreams; a shaman should be asked to perform rites of averting and yielding, and then the medicine will work.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。这一首里读不顺的地方：「月建值末各小吉」的「末」是「未」、「各」是「名」的误写；「浑身沉重难起例」的「例」按上下文读作倒、卧；「飞来墓杀」「卯方得病绕回转」「南北社廊鬼相衡」书里都没有解释，「相衡」译成「互相抵着」是照字面；「作崇令人谵语逢」最后一个「逢」字和下一句「板木末全凶怪梦」连不上，像是脱了字，译文把它留在句末；「板木末全」的「末」读作「未」（没有备齐），这是读法；「禳让」译成「禳解让退」也是照字面。「三焦」是中医里的三焦（上焦、中焦、下焦），书里没有展开。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. Places in this verse that do not read smoothly: in 'when the Month falls on Wei, named Xiaoji' the book prints the wrong characters for 'Wei' and for 'named', plainly misprints; 'the whole body is heavy and he can hardly rise' has a last character read from context as 'lie down' or 'fall'; the 'flying Tomb Killer', 'an illness taken in the Mao direction goes around and turns back' and 'the ghosts of the altar and the corridor in the south and north face each other' are not explained in the book, and 'face each other' is the literal sense; the final character of 'they make trouble and make the patient talk deliriously, and meeting' does not connect with the next line, 'wooden boards not complete, ominous, strange dreams', and looks as if a character has dropped out, so the translation leaves it at the end of the line; the 'not' of 'boards not complete' is printed with a character that is read as 'not yet' (not provided in full), which is a reading; 'rites of averting and yielding' is again the literal sense. The 'Triple Burner' is the Triple Burner of Chinese medicine (upper, middle and lower), which the book does not expand.

yi: 小吉当值的日子
（月建落在未上，名叫小吉，在卦上生出的事。）
小吉当值占病，主头痛；
三焦发热发闷，腹中疼痛；
全身沉重，难以起身；
飞来的墓杀最凶；
在卯方得的病，会绕一圈又转回来；
南北方向社庙、廊下的鬼互相抵着；
未宫的卦这样断：
横死的亡魂、死去的鬼，和土地；
作祟，让人说胡话，遇上
板木没有备齐，就凶，多怪梦；
请巫师禳解让退，药方才通。
en: When Xiaoji rules the day
(when the Month falls on Wei, named Xiaoji, what it gives rise to in the hexagram)
Xiaoji, divining illness: it means headache;
the Triple Burner is hot and oppressed, with pain in the belly;
the whole body is heavy and he can hardly rise;
the Tomb Killer that flies in is the most ominous;
an illness taken in the Mao direction goes around and turns back;
the ghosts of the altar and the corridor in the south and north face each other;
The verdict for the Wei-palace hexagrams:
the dead by injury, the dead ghosts, and the Earth God;
they make trouble and make the patient talk deliriously, and meeting
wooden boards not complete, it is ominous, with strange dreams;
have a shaman perform rites of averting and yielding, and the medicine will work.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·传送（月建申）占病：头痛、手脚皮肤见血光、四肢拘急不思食；灶司引外伤亡、犯冤家咒咀；申宫卦断旺神有愿急须解、醮谢星辰祭土主王

rule.yi: 月建落在申、叫传送的时候占病：头痛，手脚和皮肤上见血光，四肢抽紧，不想吃东西。作祟的是灶司引进来的外面的伤亡鬼、冤家和咒咀他的鬼，牵连到香火和家堂。「申宫卦断」那一段说：旺相的神有愿没还，赶紧要解；再适合许愿保平安，做醮酬谢星辰，在本方位祭土主王。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Shen, named Chuansong, divining illness: headache, bloodshed on the hands, feet and skin, the limbs cramped and no wish to eat. The ones at work are the dead by injury from outside whom the Kitchen Official has drawn in, enemies and the ghosts of those who cursed him, tied to the incense-fire and the family hall. The passage 'the verdict for the Shen-palace hexagrams' says: a strong spirit has a vow outstanding and it must be released quickly; it is also fitting to make a vow to keep him safe, to perform a thanksgiving offering to the stars, and to make offerings to the Earth Lord, the King, in the quarter concerned.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。标题括号里的「中月名曰傅送」，「中」是「申」、「傅」是「传」的误写。「灶司引透外伤亡」的「引透」按上下文读作引进来；「咒咀」就是咒诅；「勾连」是牵连；「土主王」书里没有解释，译成「土主王」（当地的土主、那位王），只是字面。「旺神有愿」是说某个旺相的神明有过愿没有还，书里没有说是哪个神；GLJ.11 里有几乎一样的一句。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. In the heading's bracket 'the Shen month is called Chuansong' the character printed for 'Shen' and the one for 'Chuan' are misprints. 'The Kitchen Official draws in' reads the book's 'draws through' as 'draws in' from context; 'cursed' is the book's 'curse'; 'tied to' is 'linked with'; 'the Earth Lord, the King' is not explained in the book and is only the literal sense (the local Earth Lord, that King). 'A strong spirit has a vow outstanding' means that some thriving spirit was promised something that has not been paid; the book does not say which spirit, and GLJ.11 has an almost identical line.

zh: （中月名曰傅送上卦以断七月之事）
yi: 传送当值的日子
（申月名叫传送，拿它在卦上断七月的事。）
传送当值时得病，主头痛；
手脚、皮肤上见血光；
四肢抽紧，不想吃东西；
灶司引着外面的伤亡鬼进来；
冲犯了冤家和咒咀他的鬼；
牵连到香火和家堂；
申宫的卦这样断：
旺相的神有愿没还，赶紧要解；
再适合许愿，保平安康健；
做醮酬谢星辰，求福求利；
在本方位设祭，祭土主王。
en: When Chuansong rules the day
(the Shen month is called Chuansong; use it with the hexagram to judge the matters of the seventh month)
an illness under Chuansong means headache;
bloodshed shows on the hands, feet and skin;
the limbs are cramped and he has no wish to eat;
the Kitchen Official draws in the dead by injury from outside;
he has offended enemies and the ghosts of those who cursed him;
it is tied to the incense-fire and the family hall;
The verdict for the Shen-palace hexagrams:
a strong spirit has a vow outstanding, and it must be released quickly;
it is also fitting to make a vow, to keep him safe and well;
perform a thanksgiving offering to the stars and ask for blessing and benefit;
set out offerings in the quarter concerned to the Earth Lord, the King.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·从魁（月建酉）占病：肺经炎如青蛇过竹筒、呕吐食不能通、寒热头疼；酉宫卦断犯天罗地网杀、家先十朝、怪神入宅宜设祭则沉病脱体

rule.yi: 月建落在酉、叫从魁的时候占病：肺经发炎，像青蛇钻过竹筒，节节生忧，药难用上；呕吐，吃下去的东西又翻出来；忽冷忽热、头疼、心神不定；病退了一下，吃药也没有功效。「酉宫卦断」那一段说：冲犯了天罗地网煞，家先和十朝都在里面；怪神进了宅，适合设祭，设了祭，沉重的病就像风一样脱身而去。
rule.en: When the Month falls on You, named Congkui, divining illness: the lung channel is inflamed, like a green snake passing through a bamboo tube, with worry at every joint and medicine hard to use; he retches and vomits and the food comes back; chills and fever, headache and a restless heart; even when it recedes for a time, taking medicine has no effect. The passage 'the verdict for the You-palace hexagrams' says: he has offended the Heaven's-Net and Earth's-Net Killer, with the household ancestors and the Ten Courts in it; uncanny spirits have entered the house and it is fitting to set out offerings, and then the deep illness leaves the body like the wind.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。标题括号「月建值如从上卦酉爻主八月事」里的「如从」两字不通，按上下文像是「从魁」写错了，译文照「酉=从魁」读，这是读法。「肺经炎」的「炎」在这本书里别处常是「灾」的误写，但这里和「青蛇过竹筒」「呕」「寒热」放在一起，读作肺经发炎（发热）更顺，仍是读法。「嗤呕」的「嗤」不知本字，按上下文读作呕吐一类；「近退」译成「刚退下去一点」是照字面。「十朝」书里没有解释，下一首说「十朝鬼判宫」，像是阴间十殿一类，译文照写「十朝」，不下定义。「天罗地网煞」是一种凶煞，书里没有解释。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. In the heading's bracket 'when the Month falls on ... the You line governs the matters of the eighth month' the two characters rendered 'on ... Congkui' do not make sense as printed and look like a miswriting of 'Congkui', and the translation reads 'You = Congkui', which is a reading. The 'inflamed' of 'the lung channel is inflamed' is elsewhere in this book often a misprint for 'calamity', but placed beside 'a green snake passing through a bamboo tube', 'retching' and 'chills and fever' it reads better as the lung channel being inflamed (hot), again a reading. The first character of 'retches' is not known as a word and is read from context as retching or vomiting; 'recedes a little' is the literal sense of 'nearly recedes'. The book does not explain 'the Ten Courts', and the next verse says 'the ghost judge's palace of the Ten Courts', which looks like the Ten Courts of the underworld, and the translation writes 'the Ten Courts' without defining them. 'The Heaven's-Net and Earth's-Net Killer' is a kind of fierce killer, not explained in the book.

zh: （月建值如从上卦酉爻主八月事）
yi: 从魁当值的日子
（月建落在酉（从魁）上，在卦上看酉爻，管八月的事。）
从魁当值占病，肺经发炎；
就像青蛇钻过竹筒；
节节都是忧患，药难用上；
呕吐，吃下的东西又翻出来，通不下去；
忽冷忽热，头疼，心神不定；
病刚退下去一点，吃药也没有功效；
酉宫的卦这样断：
冲犯了天罗地网煞；
家先和十朝都在里面；
怪神进了宅，适合设祭；
沉重的病就脱身而去，像风一样。
en: When Congkui rules the day
(when the Month falls on You, Congkui, look at the You line in the hexagram: it governs the matters of the eighth month)
Congkui, divining illness: the lung channel is inflamed;
just like a green snake passing through a bamboo tube;
worry arises at every joint and medicine is hard to use;
he retches and vomits, the food comes back, and nothing passes through;
chills and fever, headache, a restless heart;
even when it recedes a little, taking medicine has no effect;
The verdict for the You-palace hexagrams:
he has offended the Heaven's-Net and Earth's-Net Killer;
the household ancestors and the Ten Courts are in it;
uncanny spirits have entered the house and it is fitting to set out offerings;
and the deep illness leaves the body like the wind.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·河魁（月建戌）占病：难安如行船下急滩、烦闷呕逆、头疼作热加寒、骨节拘急；戌宫卦断日中出路骂神鬼、社司咒咀、退西方五墓煞

rule.yi: 月建落在戌、叫河魁的时候占病：难以安稳，像行船冲下急滩；心里烦闷，又呕吐上逆；头疼发热，有时又加上发冷；四肢骨节更加拘紧。冲犯的是十朝的鬼判宫。「戌宫卦断」那一段说：白天在路上骂过神鬼，社司的咒咀名目很多，要把西方的五墓煞退送出去，免得病人的身体重得像山。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Xu, named Hekui, divining illness: he cannot be at ease, like a boat running down a rapid; the heart is vexed and oppressed, with retching and counterflow; headache with fever, sometimes with chills added; the joints of the limbs are more cramped still. What has been offended is the ghost judge's palace of the Ten Courts. The passage 'the verdict for the Xu-palace hexagrams' says: he cursed spirits and ghosts on the road at midday, the curses of the Altar Official come in many kinds, and the Five-Tombs Killer of the west is to be driven back, lest the sick body grow heavy as a mountain.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。「日中出路骂神鬼」的「日中」译成白天、中午，「出路」译成在路上，都是照字面。「番退」的「番」读作翻，「番退西方五墓煞」译成「翻转退送」，书里没有给做法。「五墓煞」是一种凶煞，书里没有解释。「十朝鬼判宫」见 LY.ILL.GLJ.04 的说明。这一首在原文里和下一首登明挨在同一行里，没有分行。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. 'Midday' for the book's 'in the middle of the day' and 'on the road' for 'goes out on the road' follow the letter. The 'turned back' of 'the Five-Tombs Killer of the west is to be turned back' reads the book's 'turn' as 'overturn', and the book does not give a method. 'The Five-Tombs Killer' is a kind of fierce killer, not explained in the book. For 'the ghost judge's palace of the Ten Courts' see the note to LY.ILL.GLJ.04. In the original this verse and the next, Dengming, run on in the same line without a break.

zh: （月建值戌名河魁主九月之事）
yi: 河魁当值的日子
（月建落在戌上，名叫河魁，管九月的事。）
河魁当值占病，主难以安稳；
就像行船冲下急滩；
心里烦闷，又呕吐上逆；
头疼发热，有时又加上发冷；
四肢骨节更加拘紧；
冲犯了十朝的鬼判宫；
戌宫的卦这样断：
白天在路上骂过神鬼；
社司的咒咀，名目又多；
要把西方的五墓煞翻转退送出去；
免得病人的身体重得像山。
en: When Hekui rules the day
(when the Month falls on Xu, named Hekui, it governs the matters of the ninth month)
Hekui, divining illness: it means he cannot be at ease;
just like a boat running down a rapid;
the heart is vexed and oppressed, and there is retching and counterflow;
headache with fever, or chills added;
the joints of the limbs are more cramped still;
he has offended the ghost judge's palace of the Ten Courts;
The verdict for the Xu-palace hexagrams:
he cursed spirits and ghosts on the road at midday;
the curses of the Altar Official come in many kinds;
the Five-Tombs Killer of the west is to be turned back and driven off;
lest the sick body grow heavy as a mountain.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·登明（月建亥）占病：颠狂、乱言、寒热头疼、对神见鬼；触犯山司木下、暗昧女伤亡；亥宫卦断半天午酉草野鬼、子时得疾难安好

rule.yi: 月建落在亥、叫登明的时候占病：癫狂，躺在床上乱说话，忽冷忽热、头疼，心里郁结，对着神像看见鬼，怪异得很。冲犯的是山司和木下，还有暗昧的女性伤亡鬼。「亥宫卦断」那一段说：半空的、午酉方位的、野外的鬼，也是家里的二姓郎；子时得的病难以安好，要赶紧保祷，免得惶恐。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Hai, named Dengming, divining illness: madness, babbling in his bed, chills and fever, headache, a knot in the heart, seeing ghosts when facing the spirits, uncanny beyond measure. What has been offended is the Mountain Official and the one under the wood, and there are obscure women dead by injury. The passage 'the verdict for the Hai-palace hexagrams' says: the ghosts of the half-sky, of Wu and You, and of the wild fields, and also the household's 'two-surname lord'; an illness taken at the Zi hour is hard to settle, and he should be quickly prayed for, to spare him distress.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。「乱言论语」是乱说话；「木下」「山司」书里没有解释，译文只照字面；「暗昧女伤亡」是说暗中、昏昧的女性伤亡鬼，也是字面；「半天午酉并草野」「二姓郎」不知所指，译文照字面写，不下定义（第 11 首有「家先三五郎」，「郎」像是民间称某类神鬼的叫法，这是推测）；「子时得疾」是说这个病是在子时得的；「保忧」两字不通，译成「保祷」是读法，像是「保佑」「保安」一类，「栖惶」是惶惑不安。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. 'Babbles confusedly' is the book's 'speaks in disorder'; 'the one under the wood' and 'the Mountain Official' are not explained in the book and are only literal; 'obscure women dead by injury' is the sense of women in the dark and the dim who died by injury, again literal; 'the half-sky, Wu and You, and the wild fields' and 'two-surname lord' are not known and are written literally without defining them (verse 11 has 'the household ancestors and the Third and Fifth Lords', and 'lord' looks like a popular name for a kind of spirit, which is a guess); 'an illness taken at the Zi hour' says that this illness was taken at the Zi hour; the two characters of 'guard against worry' do not make sense as printed, and 'prayed for' is a reading, as if it were 'protect' or 'keep safe', while 'distress' is the book's word for being unsettled and perplexed.

yi: 登明当值的日子
（月建是亥，名叫登明，管十月的事。）
登明当值得病，主癫狂；
躺在床上乱说话；
忽冷忽热，头疼，心里郁结；
对着神像看见鬼，怪异得很；
冲犯了山司和木下；
还有暗昧的女性伤亡鬼；
亥宫的卦这样断：
半空的、午酉方位的、野外的鬼；
也是家里的二姓郎；
子时得的病，难以安好；
赶紧要保祷，免得忧虑惶恐。
en: When Dengming rules the day
(the Month at Hai is named Dengming and governs the matters of the tenth month)
Dengming, falling ill: it means madness;
he babbles confusedly in his high bed;
chills and fever, headache, a knot in the heart;
facing the spirits he sees ghosts, uncanny beyond measure;
he has offended the Mountain Official and the one under the wood;
and there are also obscure women dead by injury;
The verdict for the Hai-palace hexagrams:
the ghosts of the half-sky, of Wu and You, and of the wild fields;
and also the household's 'two-surname lord';
an illness taken at the Zi hour is hard to settle;
he should be quickly prayed for, to spare him worry and distress.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·神后（月建子）占病：虚惊、寒热、腹中疾痛及肝心、浑身沉重、四肢疼痛；子宫卦断不思饮食又番吐、触犯山神土石精、宜禳土杀神及伤亡五道

rule.yi: 月建落在子、叫神后的时候占病：虚惊，白天得病是鬼来侵犯；寒热时来，很蹊跷；腹中疼痛，牵连肝和心；全身沉重，转不了身；四肢疼痛，不能安宁。「子宫卦断」那一段说：不想吃喝，又翻着吐；冲犯了山神和土石精；手脚疼痛，一动就气喘，适合禳解土杀神；还有伤亡鬼和五道，要祈求、做福事，保平安。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Zi, named Shenhou, divining illness: a false alarm; an illness taken in the daytime is a ghost's invasion; chills and fever come at times and are very odd; pain in the belly, reaching the liver and the heart; the whole body heavy and unable to turn; the limbs ache and cannot settle. The passage 'the verdict for the Zi-palace hexagrams' says: no wish for food or drink, and vomiting again and again; he has offended the Mountain Spirit and the earth-and-stone sprites; the hands and feet ache and movement leaves him short of breath, and it is fitting to perform rites against the Earth-Killer spirits; there are also the dead by injury and the Five Ways, and he should pray and perform blessing rites to keep himself in peace.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。「日中得病」的「日中」译成白天；「远跷蹊」的「远」不知本字，按上下文读作很；「四肢疼痛末能安」的「末」读作「未」（不能）；「手足疾疼举动」和「气急宜禳土杀神」在原文里隔着一个空格，像是脱了字，译文把「举动气急」连着读（一动就气喘），这是读法；「土杀神」「五道」「土石精」书里都没有解释，译文只照字面。「神后值卦主虚惊」的「虚惊」是说受惊吓而无事，书里没有展开。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. 'In the daytime' is the book's 'in the middle of the day'; the first character of 'very odd' is not known as a word and is read from context as 'very'; 'cannot settle' reads the book's 'has not yet been able to settle' with the character for 'not yet' standing for 'cannot'; 'the hands and feet ache and movement' and 'short of breath, it is fitting to perform rites against the Earth-Killer spirits' are separated by a space in the original, as if a character had dropped out, and the translation reads 'movement ... short of breath' straight on (a movement leaves him gasping), which is a reading; 'the Earth-Killer spirits', 'the Five Ways' and 'the earth-and-stone sprites' are not explained in the book and are only literal. The 'false alarm' of 'it means a false alarm' says being frightened with no harm to follow, and the book does not expand it.

zh: （月建值子名神后主十一月事）
yi: 神后当值的日子
（月建落在子上，名叫神后，管十一月的事。）
神后当值，主虚惊；
白天得的病，是鬼来侵犯；
寒热不时地来，很蹊跷；
腹中疼痛，牵连到肝和心；
全身沉重，转不了身；
四肢疼痛，不能安宁；
子宫的卦这样断：
不想吃喝，又翻着吐；
冲犯了山神和土石精；
手脚疼痛，一动就气喘；
适合禳解土杀神；
还有伤亡鬼和五道；
祈求，做福事，保平安。
en: When Shenhou rules the day
(when the Month falls on Zi, named Shenhou, it governs the matters of the eleventh month)
when Shenhou rules the hexagram it means a false alarm;
an illness taken in the daytime is a ghost's invasion;
chills and fever come at times, and are very odd;
pain in the belly, reaching the liver and the heart;
the whole body is heavy and cannot turn;
the limbs ache and cannot settle;
The verdict for the Zi-palace hexagrams:
no wish for food or drink, and vomiting again and again;
he has offended the Mountain Spirit and the earth-and-stone sprites;
the hands and feet ache and movement leaves him short of breath;
it is fitting to perform rites against the Earth-Killer spirits;
there are also the dead by injury and the Five Ways;
pray, perform blessing rites, and keep him in peace.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·大吉（月建丑）占病：胸肋、寒热、大小便不通、不思饭食心中结；伏尸古墓同为祸；丑宫卦断社司五朝入宅、更犯五道伤亡、退北方凶恶杀、禳谢本命星辰

rule.yi: 月建落在丑、叫大吉的时候占病：胸和肋疼，有时发冷有时发热，大小便都不通，不想吃饭，心里郁结。伏尸和古墓一同作祸，只是家先牵着引着。「丑宫卦断」那一段说：社司、五朝进了宅，要设祭给香火和土地；又冲犯了五道和伤亡鬼，要把北方的凶恶煞退送出去，向本命上的星辰禳解酬谢，化解流年的灾病厄运。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Chou, named Daji, divining illness: the chest and ribs, now chills and now fever, neither urine nor stool passing, no wish for food, a knot in the heart. The Hidden Corpse and the ancient tomb make trouble together, only that the household ancestors lead them through and receive them. The passage 'the verdict for the Chou-palace hexagrams' says: the Altar Official and the Five Courts have entered the house, and offerings are to be set out to the incense-fire and the Earth God; the Five Ways and the dead by injury have also been offended, the fierce killer of the north is to be driven off, rites and thanks are to be made to the stars of his natal destiny, and the calamity, illness and misfortune of the passing year resolved.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。「伏尸古墓」的「伏尸」书里没有解释，按字面是暗藏的尸；「家先透引接」读作家先牵引着、接应着（那些鬼），是读法；「五朝」不知所指，像是和「十朝」（见 GLJ.04）同类的叫法，不下定义；「小便大便已不通」的「已」读作都；「解释」是化解，不是解说。「本命上星辰」是病人本命（出生年）对应的星辰。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. The book does not explain 'the Hidden Corpse', which literally is a corpse lying in hiding; 'the household ancestors lead them through and receive them' reads the book's 'lead through and receive' as the ancestors leading and meeting those ghosts, which is a reading; what 'the Five Courts' are is not known, and they look like a kind of thing with the 'Ten Courts' (see GLJ.04), and are not defined; the 'neither' of 'neither urine nor stool passes' reads the book's 'already' as 'both'; 'resolve' is the book's 'release', in the sense of undoing, not of explaining. 'The stars of his natal destiny' are the stars answering to the patient's natal year.

zh: （月建值丑名大吉主十二月事）
yi: 大吉当值的日子
（月建落在丑上，名叫大吉，管十二月的事。）
大吉当值占病，主胸和肋；
有时发冷，有时发热；
大小便都不通；
不想吃饭，心里郁结；
伏尸和古墓一同作祸；
只是家先牵着引着接着；
丑宫的卦这样断：
社司、五朝进了宅；
对香火、土地，要设祭；
又冲犯了五道和伤亡鬼；
要把北方的凶恶煞退送出去；
向本命上的星辰禳解酬谢；
化解流年的灾病厄运。
en: When Daji rules the day
(when the Month falls on Chou, named Daji, it governs the matters of the twelfth month)
Daji, divining illness: it means the chest and the ribs;
now chills come, now fever;
neither urine nor stool passes;
no wish for food, a knot in the heart;
the Hidden Corpse and the ancient tomb make trouble together;
only that the household ancestors lead them through and receive them;
The verdict for the Chou-palace hexagrams:
the Altar Official and the Five Courts have entered the house;
to the incense-fire and the Earth God, ask for offerings to be set out;
the Five Ways and the dead by injury have also been offended;
the fierce killer of the north is to be driven off;
make rites and thanks to the stars of his natal destiny;
and resolve the calamity, illness and misfortune of the passing year.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·功曹（月建寅）占病：白虎神、寒热头痛、胸肋疼闷气冲心、手足拘攀行不得；触犯山司木下神；寅宫卦断伤亡五道东北土煞怪巽入宅、禳度即安轻

rule.yi: 月建落在寅、叫功曹的时候占病：功曹当值，是白虎神，要赶紧祭祀超度，免得有哭声；病人忽冷忽热，头疼，胸肋疼闷，气往上冲心，手脚拘挛，走不动。冲犯的是山司和木下神。「寅宫卦断」那一段说：还有伤亡鬼和五道，东北方的土煞又加上来，怪巽进了宅作祸；只要做禳解超度，马上安稳减轻。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Yin, named Gongcao, divining illness: when Gongcao rules the day it is the White Tiger spirit, and offerings and deliverance should be made at once, to avoid the sound of weeping; the sick person has chills and fever, a headache, the chest and ribs aching and oppressed with breath surging against the heart, and the hands and feet drawn and cramped so that he cannot walk. What has been offended is the Mountain Official and the spirit under the wood. The passage 'the verdict for the Yin-palace hexagrams' says: there are also the dead by injury and the Five Ways, the Earth Killer of the northeast comes on top, and the uncanny Xun has come into the house to make trouble; if rites of averting and deliverance are performed, he is soon at ease and lighter.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。这一首的头一句「功曹值日白虎神」是十二首里唯一直接点出六神的，把功曹和白虎神连在一起，书里没有说为什么。「拘攀」读作拘挛；「怪巽」书里没有解释，「巽」是八卦里的巽（东南），像是说东南方来的怪，是读法；最后一句「世须禳度」的「世」字不通，像是「但」或「只」的误写，译文按「只要」读，这是读法；「安轻」是安稳、减轻。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. The first line of this verse, 'when Gongcao rules the day, there is the White Tiger spirit', is the only one among the twelve that names one of the six spirits directly, tying Gongcao to the White Tiger, and the book does not say why. 'Drawn and cramped' reads the book's word for being drawn and clutching as 'cramped'; the book does not explain 'the uncanny Xun', where 'Xun' is the Xun of the eight trigrams (southeast), and it looks like an uncanny thing coming from the southeast, which is a reading; in the last line the first character of 'if rites of averting and deliverance are performed' does not make sense as printed and looks like a miswriting of 'only' or 'but', and the translation reads it as 'if', which is a reading; 'at ease and lighter' is 'settled and eased'.

yi: 功曹当值的日子
（月建落在寅上，名叫功曹，管正月的事。）
功曹值日，是白虎神；
赶紧祭祀超度，免得有哭声；
病人忽冷忽热，头疼；
胸肋疼闷，气往上冲心；
手脚拘挛，走不动；
冲犯了山司和木下神；
寅宫的卦这样断：
还有伤亡鬼和五道；
东北方的土煞又加上来；
怪巽进了宅作祸；
只要做禳解超度，马上安稳减轻。
en: When Gongcao rules the day
(when the Month falls on Yin, named Gongcao, it governs the matters of the first month)
when Gongcao rules the day, there is the White Tiger spirit;
quickly make offerings and deliverance, to avoid the sound of weeping;
the sick person has chills and fever and an aching head;
the chest and ribs ache and are oppressed, with breath surging against the heart;
the hands and feet are drawn and cramped, and he cannot walk;
he has offended the Mountain Official and the spirit under the wood;
The verdict for the Yin-palace hexagrams:
there are also the dead by injury and the Five Ways;
the Earth Killer of the northeast comes on top;
the uncanny Xun has come into the house to make trouble;
if rites of averting and deliverance are performed, he is soon at ease and lighter.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·太冲（月建卯）占病：在路头充着游瘟、寒热心头闷、脚手酸疼难动；四野伤亡作祸；卯宫卦断土主社司河神水鬼、急宜禳谢身康吉不须服药

rule.yi: 月建落在卯、叫太冲的时候占病：病是在路口上得的，撞上了游瘟，作祸生忧；有时冷有时热，心口闷，手脚酸疼，难以走动；是野外的伤亡鬼来作祸，要化解咒咀免得结成冤仇。「卯宫卦断」那一段说：土主、社司要设祭，河神、水鬼使病缠着不走；赶紧禳解酬谢，身体就康健吉利，不用吃药，自然没有忧愁。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Mao, named Taichong, divining illness: it was taken at the head of the road, having run into the Wandering Plague, which makes trouble and worry; now cold, now hot, oppression at the heart, the hands and feet aching and sore so that he can hardly move about; the dead by injury of the open fields have come to make trouble, and the curses are to be resolved so that they do not turn to enmity. The passage 'the verdict for the Mao-palace hexagrams' says: the Earth Lord and the Altar Official should be given offerings, and the River Spirit and the water ghosts make the illness linger; quickly perform rites and thanks and the body will be healthy and fortunate, with no need of medicine, and there will be no worry.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。标题括号里「太衡」是「太冲」的误写。「充着」读作冲着、撞上；「游瘟」是四处游走传播瘟疫的神鬼，书里没有展开；「作淹留」是使人久病、拖着不走。这一首最后两句「不须服药自无愁」是十二首里唯一直接说不用吃药的（第 2 首说「药方通」，要请巫师做了法事药才有用），两首的态度不一样，书里没有说明。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. In the heading's bracket the printed 'Taiheng' is a misprint for 'Taichong'. 'Ran into' reads the book's 'charge against' as running up against; 'the Wandering Plague' is a spirit that wanders about spreading plague, which the book does not expand; 'make the illness linger' is the book's 'make him detained', that is, keep the illness on and not let it go. The last line of this verse, 'no medicine is needed, and there will be no worry', is the only one among the twelve that says outright that medicine is not needed (verse 2 says 'the medicine will work' once a shaman has performed the rites, so that medicine works only after the rites), and the two take different attitudes, which the book does not discuss.

zh: （月建值卯名太衡主二月之事）
yi: 太冲当值的日子
（月建落在卯上，名叫太冲，管二月的事。）
太冲当值占病，病是在路口上得的；
撞上了游瘟，作祸生忧；
有时冷有时热，心口闷；
手脚酸疼，难以走动；
野外的伤亡鬼来作祸；
化解咒咀，免得结成冤仇；
卯宫的卦这样断：
土主、社司，要设祭；
河神、水鬼，使病缠着不走；
赶紧禳解酬谢，身体就康健吉利；
不用吃药，自然没有忧愁。
en: When Taichong rules the day
(when the Month falls on Mao, named Taichong, it governs the matters of the second month)
Taichong, divining illness: it was taken at the head of the road;
he ran into the Wandering Plague, which makes trouble and worry;
now cold, now hot, with oppression at the heart;
the hands and feet ache and are sore and he can hardly move about;
the dead by injury of the open fields come to make trouble;
resolve the curses so that they do not turn to enmity;
The verdict for the Mao-palace hexagrams:
the Earth Lord and the Altar Official: ask for offerings to be set out;
the River Spirit and the water ghosts make the illness linger;
quickly perform rites and thanks and the body will be healthy and fortunate;
no medicine is needed, and there will be no worry.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·天罡（月建辰）占病：心腹膨胀卧高床、寒热往来须作痛；天罗地网煞山司木下廊边鬼；辰宫卦断半天午酉降祸、家先三五郎、旺神有愿急解谢、退送墓煞

rule.yi: 月建落在辰、叫天罡的时候占病：这天得的病，心腹胀满，卧在床上，寒热交替，必定疼痛。作祟的是天罗地网煞，山司、木下、廊边的鬼，还有正通和伤亡鬼。「辰宫卦断」那一段说：半空的、午酉方位的鬼一同降祸，还有家先和三郎、五郎；旺相的神有愿没还，赶紧解愿酬谢，把墓煞退送出去，免得病人惶恐不安。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Chen, named Tiangang, divining illness: an illness taken on this day, the heart and belly swollen, lying in his bed, chills and fever alternating, bound to be painful. The ones at work are the Heaven's-Net and Earth's-Net Killer, the Mountain Official, the one under the wood and the ghosts by the corridor, and also the Zhengtong and the dead by injury. The passage 'the verdict for the Chen-palace hexagrams' says: the ghosts of the half-sky and of Wu and You send down misfortune together, and there are also the household ancestors and the Third and Fifth Lords; a strong spirit has a vow outstanding, and it is to be released quickly with thanks, and the Tomb Killer sent away, to spare the sick person distress.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。「此日得病值天」这一句只有六个字，像是脱了「罡」字（天罡），译文把这一点写在括号里，是读法。「正通」书里没有解释，有可能是「五通」（民间的一种神）之误，但原文没有说，译文只照字面写「正通」。「廊边鬼」「三五郎」（三郎、五郎）「半天午酉」书里都没有解释；「墓煞」是一种凶煞。「旺神有愿」同 GLJ.03。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. The line 'an illness taken on this day falls upon Heaven' has only six characters and looks as if the character for 'Gang' (Tiangang) has dropped out, and the translation puts this in brackets, which is a reading. The book does not explain 'the Zhengtong', and it may be a miswriting of 'the Wutong' (a kind of popular spirit), but the original does not say so, and the translation writes 'the Zhengtong' literally. 'The ghosts by the corridor', 'the Third and Fifth Lords' and 'the half-sky, Wu and You' are not explained in the book; 'the Tomb Killer' is a kind of fierce killer. For 'a strong spirit has a vow outstanding' see GLJ.03.

zh: （月建值辰名天罡主三月之事）
yi: 天罡当值的日子
（月建落在辰上，名叫天罡，管三月的事。）
这一天得的病，值上了天（罡）；
心腹胀满，卧在床上；
寒热交替，必定疼痛；
天罗地网煞作祸；
山司、木下、廊边的鬼；
还有正通和伤亡鬼；
辰宫的卦这样断：
半空的、午酉方位的鬼一同降祸；
还有家先和三郎、五郎；
旺相的神有愿没还，赶紧解愿酬谢；
把墓煞退送出去，免得惶恐不安。
en: When Tiangang rules the day
(when the Month falls on Chen, named Tiangang, it governs the matters of the third month)
an illness taken on this day falls upon 'Heaven' (the line is short of a character, probably Tiangang);
the heart and belly swell, and he lies in his bed;
chills and fever alternate, and there is bound to be pain;
the Heaven's-Net and Earth's-Net Killer brings harm;
the Mountain Official, the one under the wood, and the ghosts by the corridor;
and also the Zhengtong and the dead by injury;
The verdict for the Chen-palace hexagrams:
the ghosts of the half-sky and of Wu and You send down misfortune together;
and there are also the household ancestors and the Third and Fifth Lords;
a strong spirit has a vow outstanding: quickly release it and give thanks;
send off the Tomb Killer and spare him distress.

chapter: 卷五·论十月将值日要决
title: 月将值日·太乙（月建巳）占病：病是两蛇、途中惊恐、心腹疼痛气冲急、男轻女重；已宫卦断触犯香堂土地、溪河落水作寒邪、四片板木皆有、病人火里出莲花

rule.yi: 月建落在巳、叫太乙的时候占病：太乙日得的病，是两条蛇作祟，在路上受了惊吓，招来祸邪；心腹疼痛，气往上冲、急促，男的轻、女的重，手脚还有血光之灾，有咒咀和口舌。「巳宫卦断」那一段说：冲犯了香堂和土地，溪河、落水的鬼作寒邪；四片板木都齐备了，病人就像火里长出莲花。
rule.en: When the Month falls on Si, named Taiyi, divining illness: an illness on a Taiyi day is the work of two snakes, a fright on the road has drawn in misfortune and evil; the heart and belly ache with the breath surging and hurried, light in a man and heavy in a woman, and there is also the calamity of bloodshed on the hands and feet, with curses and quarrels. The passage 'the verdict for the Si-palace hexagrams' says: he has offended the incense hall and the Earth God, and the ghosts of streams and rivers and of the drowned make cold evil; once the four wooden boards are all there, the sick person is like a lotus coming out of the fire.

note.yi: 格式和名词见 LY.ILL.GLJ.01。标题括号里「月建值已」「已宫卦断」的「已」是「巳」的误写；「脚手血光炎更有」的「炎」读作「灾」（这本书里别处常把「灾」写成「炎」），是读法；「神广咒咀」的「神广」不知所指，译文照字面写；「口牙」读作口舌（争吵），同书别处也有「寻君起口牙」的说法；「男轻女重最交加」是说男的轻、女的重、轻重夹杂，书里没有展开；「四片板木皆有已」的「已」字不通，按上下文读作「已经」，整句读作四片板木齐备了（同 GLJ.01 的「板木来全」），是读法；「火里出莲花」是说在绝境里转好，书里没有注。十二首到这一首为止；原文这一行末尾还连着下一部分的标题「精校断易鬼灵经」，不收。
note.en: For the form and the terms see LY.ILL.GLJ.01. In the heading's brackets 'the Month falls on Si' and 'the Si-palace' the printed character is a misprint of 'Si'; the 'calamity' of 'the calamity of bloodshed on the hands and feet' is read from a character printed 'inflamed' (this book often writes 'calamity' that way), which is a reading; 'Shenguang' is not known and is written literally; 'quarrels' is the book's 'mouth and teeth', which the book uses elsewhere too, as in 'come looking for you and stir up mouth-and-teeth'; 'light in a man, heavy in a woman, all mixed together' says light in a man, heavy in a woman, light and heavy mingled, and the book does not expand it; the last character of 'the four wooden boards are all there' does not make sense as printed and is read from context as 'already', so that the whole line reads that the four boards have been made ready (as with 'the wooden boards come, complete' in GLJ.01), which is a reading; 'a lotus coming out of the fire' says that things turn for the better out of a desperate pass, and the book gives no comment. The twelve verses end here; the end of this line in the original runs into the heading of the next part, 'the carefully collated Duanyi Guiling Jing', which is not quoted.

zh: （月建值已名太乙主四月之事）
yi: 太乙当值的日子
（月建落在巳上，名叫太乙，管四月的事。）
太乙日得的病，是两条蛇作祟；
在路上受惊吓，招来祸邪；
心腹疼痛，气往上冲，急促；
男的轻，女的重，最是夹杂；
手脚的血光之灾也有；
神广、咒咀，有口舌；
巳宫的卦这样断：
冲犯了香堂和土地；
溪河、落水的鬼作寒邪；
四片板木都有了；
病人就像火里长出莲花。
en: When Taiyi rules the day
(when the Month falls on Si, named Taiyi, it governs the matters of the fourth month)
an illness on a Taiyi day is the work of two snakes;
a fright on the road has drawn in misfortune and evil;
the heart and belly ache, the breath surging and hurried;
light in a man, heavy in a woman, all mixed together;
the calamity of bloodshed on the hands and feet is also found;
'Shenguang', curses and quarrels;
The verdict for the Si-palace hexagrams:
he has offended the incense hall and the Earth God;
the ghosts of streams and rivers and of the drowned make cold evil;
once the four wooden boards are all there;
the sick person is like a lotus coming out of the fire.

title: 鬼入六神断决·占病：鬼入青龙病渐轻；鬼入朱雀身命危宜求谢；鬼入白虎占病急去买棺材；鬼入玄武占病昏睡耳聋

rule.yi: 官鬼落在六神上，各有各的断法，占病时：鬼入青龙，病渐渐轻了，是堂前讨吃的亡人，或死在外面回来作怪的鬼；鬼入朱雀，身家性命危险，是伤亡鬼、五道，适合祈求酬谢，不谢会损害病人；鬼入白虎，哭声哀哀，占病的话赶紧去买棺材，秋冬多精怪，要提防老人和小孩；鬼入玄武，必定凶，占病昏睡耳聋，是落水死的、伤亡的鬼来讨吃的，赶紧保祷酬谢。
rule.en: Pressure falling on each of the six spirits has its own judgment, and in divining illness: Pressure in Azure Dragon, the illness gradually lightens, and it is a dead person asking for food in front of the hall, or one who died outside and has come back to make trouble; Pressure in Vermilion Bird, his person and life are in danger, it is the dead by injury and the Five Ways, and it is fitting to pray and give thanks, for without thanks the sick body is harmed; Pressure in White Tiger, mournful weeping, and in divining illness go quickly and buy the coffin, in autumn and winter there are many sprites, and one should guard the old and the young; Pressure in Dark Tortoise, surely ominous, in divining illness he sleeps heavily and is deaf, the drowned and the dead by injury come asking for food, and he should quickly pray and give thanks.

note.yi: 这一组在书里有六首（青龙、朱雀、勾陈、螣蛇、白虎、玄武），这里只收四首，因为勾陈那首（「弟兄求」「公婆也容只见愁」）和螣蛇那首没有讲到病，螣蛇那首的字句又残缺不通（「鬼入蛇你莫夸 外面更有神 冤家 不时有愿前时穴 更有宅居有些些」），译不出来，不收。书里的「鬼」就是官鬼那一爻，同时也指它代表的鬼；译文第一次出现写「Pressure」，说「鬼里有人」「亡人」时指鬼魂。「求食」是亡魂来讨祭祀的饭食（要给它祭）；「梦魂精」不知所指，按字面写；「保谢」是保祷酬谢；「须防老幼免心怀」的「心怀」读作挂心，这句不很通，是读法。这四首里直接讲病轻重生死的是：青龙「病渐轻」，朱雀「身命危」，白虎「占病急去买棺材」，玄武「占病昏睡耳又聋」。
note.en: This group has six verses in the book (Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, Hook Earth, Coiling Snake, White Tiger, Dark Tortoise), and only four are taken here, because the Hook Earth verse ('seeking brothers', 'the in-laws too can only see sorrow') and the Coiling Snake verse do not speak of illness, and the Coiling Snake verse is also broken and does not make sense (it reads, roughly, 'Pressure enters the snake, you must not boast, outside there is also a spirit, enemies, at times a vow, the earlier grave, and also something about the dwelling'), so it could not be translated and is not taken. The book's 'ghost' is the Pressure line and also the ghosts it stands for; the translation writes 'Pressure' at the first mention and 'ghost' where it says 'among the ghosts there is one' or 'a dead person'. 'Asking for food' means the dead soul has come for the sacrificial food (that is, it is to be given offerings); the book does not explain 'the soul-sprites of dreams' and the translation keeps to the letter; 'pray and give thanks' is the book's 'protect and thank'; 'to spare anxiety' reads the book's 'heart' as being anxious about it, and the line is not smooth, which is a reading. The four verses that speak directly of how light or heavy the illness is, and of life and death, are: Azure Dragon 'the illness gradually lightens', Vermilion Bird 'his person and life are in danger', White Tiger 'divining illness, go quickly and buy the coffin' and Dark Tortoise 'in divining illness he sleeps heavily and is deaf in the ears'.

yi: 鬼落在六神上的断法
en: Judgments on Pressure entering the six spirits

yi: 鬼落在青龙上
鬼入青龙，病渐渐轻了；
堂前来讨吃的，是死去的人；
鬼当中有人是死在外面的；
回来作怪，成了妖精。
en: Pressure enters Azure Dragon
Pressure in Azure Dragon: the illness gradually lightens;
the one asking for food in front of the hall is a dead person;
among the ghosts there is one who died outside;
who has come back and makes trouble as a sprite.

yi: 鬼落在朱雀上
鬼入朱雀，身家性命危险；
是伤亡鬼、五道，梦里的魂精；
适合用祈求酬谢的办法，才吉利；
如果不酬谢保祷，会损害病人的身体。
en: Pressure enters Vermilion Bird
Pressure in Vermilion Bird: his person and life are in danger;
the dead by injury, the Five Ways, the soul-sprites of dreams;
it is fitting to use prayer and thanks, and only then is it fortunate;
if the thanks and protection are not made, the sick body will be harmed.

yi: 鬼落在白虎上
鬼入白虎，哭声哀哀；
占病的话，赶紧去买棺材；
秋冬碰上的话，多有精怪；
要提防老人和小孩，免得挂心。
en: Pressure enters White Tiger
Pressure in White Tiger: mournful weeping;
in divining illness, go quickly and buy the coffin;
if it comes in autumn or winter there are many sprites;
guard the old and the young, to spare anxiety.

yi: 鬼落在玄武上
鬼入玄武，必定是凶；
占病的话，昏睡，耳朵又聋；
落水死的、伤亡的鬼来讨吃的；
赶紧保祷酬谢，免得灾祸忧患。
en: Pressure enters Dark Tortoise
Pressure in Dark Tortoise: surely ominous;
in divining illness he sleeps heavily and is deaf in the ears;
the drowned and the dead by injury come asking for food;
quickly pray and give thanks, to avoid calamity and worry.

title: 入门来听断·来问时门前所见：慌忙来问官司病者在床中；入门见老男儿病者安然无伤损；孩儿哭啼病患都皆有；入门一灯病者见凶星；三人话病者最是鸟鸡子

rule.yi: 进门的时候看到的人和物、听到的话，先断一个大概，讲到病的几句是：慌慌张张来问事，必凶，病的人躺在床上；进门先见一个老年男子，病人平安，没有损伤，像枯木碰上了春天；进门看见小孩哭哭啼啼，家里不吉利，破财、病患都有；进门见遇三个人说话，官司里官鬼发动，病人最要紧的是（见到）鸟、鸡、子之类，阎王一定要请他回去；进门见一盏灯，病人见凶星，要斋神求福，保祷度过就不相牵连；进门一炷香，家宅大吉大昌，官司马上消散，病人得以离床。
rule.en: What is seen and heard on entering the door gives a first rough judgment, and the lines that speak of illness are these: if he comes in a flurry to ask, it is surely ominous, and the sick are in bed; if an old man is seen first on entering, the sick one is safe and unharmed, like a withered tree meeting spring; if a child is seen crying on entering, the household is unlucky, and loss of money and illness are all present; if on entering he meets three people talking, then in an official matter Pressure moves, and the sick one's chief matter is (the sight of) a bird, a hen or a child, and Yama will surely call him back; if on entering he sees a lamp, the sick one meets an ominous star, and he should keep the fast to the spirits and ask for blessing, and with prayer he passes through without being dragged in; if on entering there is a stick of incense, the household is greatly fortunate and prosperous, the official matter dissolves at once, and the sick one gets up from his bed.

note.yi: 这是附录里的一首长诗，没有标点，一口气念下来，按「入门见某物」一条一条断：官司、失物、婚姻、买卖、病各条里都有几句，这里只收讲到病的六条（其余：「衣冠来问必婚姻」「入门见一鸡鸭随」「入门见宁纱」「入门见柴木」四条没有讲病，不收）。这一首的字句多处不通，译文是最接近字面的读法，不当作确切的意思：「入门是大正无悠忧」的「大正」「悠忧」，「病是凶神为福守」，「病者最是鸟鸡子」（鸟鸡子是鸟、鸡、子，还是「乌鸡子」，不能定），「齐神」（像是「斋神」），「病者得难床」（「难」疑是「离」之误，读作离床，是读法）都是这样。「病者最是鸟鸡子 阎王必要请回归」是死兆，「病者安然无伤损 如喜枯木正逢春」是吉兆；「入门见一灯」那条里「病者见凶星」后面接的是「齐神求为福 保度不相牵」，是说见凶星要去求神保祷。这里写的「入门」是问卦的人走进门来，还是医者进病家的门，书里没有说，译文写作「进门」，不定主语。
note.en: This is a long poem in the appendix, without punctuation, read off in one breath, judging item by item from 'on entering the door he sees such-and-such': each item has a few lines on a lawsuit, lost goods, marriage, trade and illness, and only the six items that speak of illness are taken here (four others, 'one who comes in robes and cap to ask is surely about marriage', 'on entering he sees a hen and a duck following', 'on entering he sees plain gauze' and 'on entering he sees firewood', do not speak of illness and are not taken). The wording of this poem does not make sense in many places, and the translation is the reading closest to the letter and is not given as the sure sense: 'greatly upright' and 'no worry' in 'on entering it is greatly upright and there is no worry', 'illness: an ominous spirit that keeps guard for blessing', 'the sick one's chief matter is a bird, a hen or a child' (whether it is a bird, a hen and a child or a 'black hen's chick' cannot be settled), 'keep the fast to the spirits' (it looks like the fast to the spirits) and 'the sick one gets up from his bed' (the character printed as 'hard' looks like a misprint of 'leave', and is read as getting up, which is a reading) are all like this. 'The sick one's chief matter is a bird, a hen or a child; Yama will surely call him back' is a sign of death, and 'the sick one is safe and unharmed, like a withered tree meeting spring' a sign of good; in the item 'on entering he sees a lamp', after 'the sick one meets an ominous star' come 'keep the fast to the spirits and ask for blessing, with prayer he passes through and is not dragged in', which says that on meeting an ominous star he should ask the spirits for protection. The book does not say whether the 'entering' is the asker coming in at the door or a healer entering the sick person's house, and the translation writes 'on entering' without fixing the subject.

yi: 进门时看到听到的断法
en: Judgments from what is seen and heard on entering the door

yi: 慌慌张张来问事，必定凶；
有官司，有病的人躺在床上；
失物找不到，生产是女孩；
纵然看着好，也让人惊疑。
en: if he comes in a flurry to ask, it is surely ominous;
a lawsuit, and the sick are in bed;
lost things are not found, and a birth is a girl;
even if it looks good, it brings fright and doubt.

yi: 进门是「大正」，没有忧愁；
有大人物搁在路上，一定不周全；
病，是凶神，也为福守着；
自然适合保祷度过，就没有忧愁。
en: on entering it is 'greatly upright', and there is no worry;
a great man blocking the road is surely not complete;
illness: an ominous spirit that keeps guard for blessing;
it is fitting to pray and pass through, and then there is no worry.

yi: 一进门就看见老年男子；
官司、失落的东西却找不到；
病人平安，没有损伤；
就像枯木正碰上春天。
en: on entering he sees at once an old man;
a lawsuit or lost goods will not be found;
the sick one is safe and unharmed;
like a withered tree meeting spring.

yi: 进门看见小孩哭哭啼啼；
家里不吉利，有损失亏耗；
破财、病患都有；
婚姻即使都办妥了也要分离。
en: on entering a child is seen crying and sobbing;
the household is unlucky, with loss and deficit;
loss of money and illness are all present;
a marriage, even when all is arranged, will part.

yi: 进门遇见三个人在说话；
官司的事，鬼动了，会怎么样；
病人最要紧的是（见到）鸟、鸡、子之类；
阎王一定要请他回去。
en: on entering he meets three people talking;
in an official matter, with Pressure moving, how will it go;
the sick one's chief matter is (the sight of) a bird, a hen or a child;
Yama will surely call him back.

yi: 进门看见一盏灯；
病人见凶星；
斋神，求福；
保祷度过，就不相牵连。
en: on entering he sees a lamp;
the sick one meets an ominous star;
keep the fast to the spirits and ask for blessing;
with prayer he passes through and is not dragged in.

yi: 进门（看见）一炷香；
家宅大吉大昌；
官司马上消散；
病人得以离床。
en: on entering, a stick of incense;
the household is greatly fortunate and prosperous;
an official matter dissolves at once;
the sick one gets up from his bed.

title: 问灾先问是何人：父母爻现是父母之病、官鬼临之怕旺相、子孙克世药无灵；财为禄命怕飞爻克、父母（印授）交重病困沉、最忌世空遇月破、又嫌墓爻发动损身

rule.yi: 占问灾病，先要问是什么人得病：父母爻出现，说的就是父母的事；官鬼临上去，愁它旺相；子孙克世爻，吃药没有灵验。财是禄命，怕被飞爻克制（原文「忘非克」，含混）；父母（印绶）交重发动，病重而困顿；最忌世爻落空又遇月破，也嫌墓爻发动伤了身体。眉批说：父亲得病要看病（官鬼）；鬼怕旺相；子克世爻，服药不灵；财是禄命，印绶发动命沉，世空、月破、墓绝都凶。
rule.en: In asking about an illness or calamity, first ask whose it is: if Resource appears, it is the parents' matter that is set out; if Pressure sits on it, one worries about its being strong; Output controlling the Self line makes medicine ineffective. Wealth is the salary and life and fears being controlled by the flying line (the text reads 'wang fei ke', which is unclear); Resource (the seal ribbon) crossing and moving heavily makes the illness heavy and trapped; most to be avoided is the Self Void together with Month-break, and the tomb line moving to harm the body is also disliked. The marginal comment says: for a father's illness, look at the illness; the ghost fears strength; if Output controls the Self line, taking medicine is ineffective; Wealth is the salary and life, the seal ribbon moving means life sinks, and the Self Void, Month-break, tomb and Extinction are all ominous.

note.yi: 这是海底眼「疾病」一节的头两首歌诀，每首后面带一条眉批。「父母逢之父母陈」的「陈」按字面译作「set out」，大意是这一爻出现就说明占的是这一层亲人；眉批「父病看病」很简，按字面译。「财为禄命忘非克」的「忘非克」不成话：下面散句（LY.ILL.HDY.02）同一句写作「忌飞克之」，所以这里按「怕被飞爻克」译，并把原字标在译文里。「印授」就是印绶，是父母爻的别名，眉批「印授命沉」按字面译作「the seal ribbon moving means life sinks」。「世空」「墓发」「墓绝」照字面译。 括号里「眉批：……」是书眉上的旁注，整理本排在正文里；这里分开收，说话人标为「海底眼眉批」。
note.en: These are the first two verses of the Haidi Yan's section on illness, each followed by a marginal comment. In 'if Resource meets it, the parents are set out' the word 'chen' is rendered literally as 'set out', the sense being that this line's appearing shows which relation the divination is about; the marginal comment 'for a father's illness, look at the illness' is very short and is rendered literally. 'Wang fei ke' in 'Wealth is the salary and life, wang fei ke' does not make sense: the prose sentence below (LY.ILL.HDY.02) writes the same sentence as 'it fears the flying line controlling it', so it is translated here as 'fears being controlled by the flying line', and the original characters are marked in the translation. 'Yin shou' is the seal ribbon, another name for the Resource line, and the marginal comment 'the seal ribbon means life sinks' is rendered literally as 'the seal ribbon moving means life sinks'. 'Self Void', 'the tomb moving' and 'tomb and Extinction' are rendered literally. The bracketed 'marginal comment' is a note from the top margin that the edited text sets in the main text; it is quoted separately here, with the speaker marked as the marginal comment.

yi: 占问灾病，先问是什么人；
父母爻遇上它，就是父母被陈说出来；
官鬼临在它上面，愁的是它旺相；
子孙克了世，吃药没有灵验。
en: In asking about a calamity, first ask who the person is;
if Resource meets it, it is the parents that are set out;
if Pressure sits on it, one worries about its being strong;
Output controlling the Self, medicine has no effect.

yi: 父亲得病，要看病；
鬼怕旺相；
子克世爻；
吃药不灵验。
en: for a father's illness, look at the illness;
the ghost fears being strong;
if Output controls the Self line;
taking medicine is not effective.

yi: 又说道：
财是禄命，怕被飞爻克制（原文作「忘非克」，含混）；
印绶交重发动，病重而困顿；
最忌世爻落空，又逢月破；
又嫌墓爻发动，伤了身体。
en: It says again:
Wealth is the salary and life, and fears being controlled by the flying line (the text reads 'wang fei ke', which is unclear);
the seal ribbon (Resource) crossing and moving heavily, the illness is heavy and trapped;
most to be avoided is the Self Void, together with Month-break;
and the tomb line moving to harm the body is also disliked.

yi: 财是禄命；
印绶发动，命就沉；
世空、月破；
墓、绝都是凶。
en: Wealth is the salary and life;
the seal ribbon moving, life sinks;
the Self Void, Month-break;
tomb and Extinction are all ominous.
